records.rationale: The diff shows LarkCalendarService's createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent using `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — Destinations without a credentialId no longer match any calendar, causing the supported legacy branch in EventManager to create events on "primary" instead of the selected destination.
records.rationale: In the Google CalendarService, selectedCalendar is now computed as destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId, falling back to 'primary'. EventManager's legacy branch (destination.credentialId falsy) calls createEvent(c, event) for all matching credentials; for such destinations no calendar in the array matches the credentialId, so the find returns undefined and events go to 'primary' instead of the previously used calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId. This is a verifiable behavioral regression introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — When externalCalendarId is missing during an update, the fallback searches for that missing value instead of a configured destination, breaking updates to existing events on secondary calendars.
records.rationale: In updateEvent the changed line reads `: event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — but this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `.find()` compares each calendar's externalId to a missing value and always returns undefined, making the fallback useless (calendarId becomes undefined). The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (the first destination). Same pattern in deleteEvent at line ~312. This is a verifiable regression introduced by the diff.

records.issue_text: The Google Calendar deletion code searches for a missing externalCalendarId instead of falling back to a configured destination, breaking the destination fallback for deletions.
records.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the diff changes the fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find predicate can never match and the fallback always yields undefined — the previous fallback to `destinationCalendar.externalId` is gone (same broken pattern in updateEvent). Deletions/updates without an explicit externalCalendarId now get no calendar id.
